title: spike: 再起動を跨いだ MCP control_request 応答の受理検証
real_claude: REQUIRED — this AC's entire purpose is to measure REAL claude CLI behavior (priority_rule 0). A fake emitter cannot answer 'how long does claude wait for a control_request response'. Must run against the real `claude` binary on this box.

acceptance_scenarios.intent: Determine whether the claude CLI's deadline for an MCP-routed permission control_request response EXCEEDS palmux2's realistic restart window (a few seconds to ~15s). If claude gives up / times out / aborts the tool before a delayed allow arrives, the ADR-0004 replay design (palmux2 answers a control_request that was in-flight across its own restart) is unsound and must be revisited.
acceptance_scenarios.test_kind: REAL-CLAUDE spike harness (Go integration harness mirroring internal/tab/claudeagent/ask_integration_test.go + bash_perm_integration_test.go real-claude wiring; env-gated like the existing real-claude integration tests). NOT a unit test, NOT a fake emitter.
steps: Build a minimal spike harness that reuses claudeagent's OWN transport primitives at the library level: spawn `claude --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages --verbose --permission-prompt-tool mcp__<server>__<tool> --settings '{"disableRemoteControl":true}'` with an in-process MCP permission server (reuse mcp.go / the PermissionRequester seam, or a hand-rolled equivalent) so we observe the EXACT wire path production uses (mcp_message control_request → can_use_tool decision).

Send a user.message that reliably forces ONE tool call requiring permission (e.g. ask claude to run a specific Bash command, or Write a file) so the CLI emits an mcp_message control_request whose inner JSON-RPC is a permission check.

Capture the timestamp the control_request arrives. Then DELIBERATELY WITHHOLD the MCP/permission response — do NOT call respondControl — for a tiered set of delays: 10s, then (fresh run) 30s, then (fresh run) 60s. Between tiers, watch stdout/stderr for any timeout/abort/error envelope, control_cancel_request, tool_result with an error, or process exit.

After each tier's delay elapses, SEND the allow response (respondControl with behavior=allow / mcp_response success) and record whether: (a) claude ACCEPTS the late response, (b) the gated tool then EXECUTES, and (c) the assistant turn CONTINUES to completion (result envelope).
Record for each tier: arrival time, whether a timeout/cancel was observed before responding, whether the late allow was accepted, whether the tool executed, and the final turn outcome.

Additionally record the OBSERVED palmux2 restart window baseline for context (how long `make serve INSTANCE=dev` kill+respawn + reconnect takes) so the deadline can be compared against the real restart pain it must survive.

Write the full result (waiting behavior, presence/absence of timeout, per-tier accept/execute/continue booleans, verdict) to docs/sprint-logs/S862203/spike-S862203-1-1.json in the same shape as docs/sprint-logs/S3f2658/spike-S3f2658-1-1.json.

GATE: if the late allow is NOT accepted (claude aborted/cancelled/timed out the control_request before ~15s, i.e. shorter than the restart window) — do NOT proceed to Story 2/3. Escalate an ADR-0004 revisit to the user per the ADR's notes (pending-request re-send by claude / ptyhost-side hold-without-auto-deny) and HALT the sprint (priority_rule 0: never false-done; escalate at milestone).
acceptance_scenarios.expected: Documented real-claude behavior. PASS = claude waits for (and accepts) a control_request response for at least the palmux2 restart window (empirically expected ≥ tens of seconds, since permission prompts are human-in-the-loop and claude blocks the turn on them) → ADR-0004 replay design confirmed sound, proceed to Wave 2. FAIL = deadline shorter than restart window → escalate ADR-0004 revisit, halt.

notes: Runs FIRST and BLOCKS Story 2 and Story 3 (they build the very replay mechanism this spike validates). Consumes real quota — keep the harness to the minimum runs needed for the three delay tiers (a handful of turns). Do NOT touch the host palmux2. The harness itself is throwaway/manual (env-gated), not part of the always-run CI suite. This spike answers the single open '-' consequence in ADR-0004 and its revisit condition verbatim.
